column3: Not a departure. The paper's proof of Lemma 2.4 reuses "the same computations" as Lemma 2.3 (Theorem 2.2 applied to X1 - X2), not Lemma 2.3's statement, which assumes n1 > n2. Both Lean proofs call that computation, packaged as dayOneAux_berryEsseen_diff (Dense/BinomialDifference.lean).

Departure (reason 1, a cited lemma applied outside its hypotheses). The paper's covariance step applies Lemma A.3 at points d <= 0 (it prints d in {0, -1}; the formal proof needs d in {-1, 0, 1}), outside its hypothesis 0 < d < (n1+n2)/2. The Lean proof uses the form of Lemma A.3 for every integer d (sparseAux_pointProb_le in Sparse/BerryEsseen.lean, from which lemmaA_3 is derived; it is the dense paper's Lemma 2.4), proved by Lemma A.3's own argument. See proposition2_2's docstring.

Not a departure. The paper's proof takes from Lemma 2.1 only its constants D_c and C(c, D) (defined in Lemma 2.1's statement) and reruns Lemma 2.1's argument (Proposition 2.2, then Chebyshev) on the active subgraph; it does not use Lemma 2.1's conclusion, which concerns the dynamics without activations. The Lean proof uses Dc and proposition2_2.

Not a departure (a misreference in the paper). In Case 2 the paper writes "By Lemma 2.6" for the bound |ac hypo B_t| <= C/(p|ac V_t|) (1-b')|ac B_t|/(1/2-b')^2, which is the first half of Lemma 2.6's proof (Lemmas 2.5, A.7 and A.4), not Lemma 2.6's statement (emptying within O(log n/log pn) days). The Lean proof uses those three lemmas; see proposition4_3's docstring.
